analysis.title: US Equities Weekly Rundown - October 30, 2026
key_insights: US stocks fell sharply Friday while the S&P 500 closed the week and month down only modestly. The market is bifurcating, with AI exposures selling off and select non-AI pockets climbing.
Obesity Drugs, Defense Spending and Biotech outperformed on the week. Bitcoin Sensitive, Software and Agentic AI underperformed.

Prime book: hedge funds net bought US equities for the first time in 4 weeks, driven by short covers in Macro Products and to a lesser extent Single Stocks. Info Tech was the most net bought sector this week through Thursday but is still heavily net sold month to date in October.
Mag 7 names collectively were net sold in 4 of the last 5 sessions, which the desk reads as little recovery in risk appetite.
Cash equities: the week began with Long Only demand in Semis and ended with an aggressive sell-off with little defense. Asset managers finished net sellers and hedge fund flows finished balanced.

Friday's selling looked systematic and top-down. ETFs were about 31% of the tape, the highest full-session level since June. Supply was concentrated in tech but was more orderly than in the prior two weeks.
S&P levels the desk is watching: 100-day moving average at 7614 and the CTA medium-term threshold at 7554.

Futures: the Russell 2000 finished the week higher and outperformed NDX and SPX despite the tech-led selloff. CFTC data through Oct 20 show net positioning rebounded from lows on new length, with sizable shorts still in place.

The Russell 2000 setup stays constrained by rate sensitivity and debt-refinancing headwinds. If Friday's price action persists, GS systematic momentum thresholds flip negative, which would halt projected CTA buying.
Derivatives: front-end vol in NDX and SPX fell sharply early in the week, with NDX 1-month fixed strike vol down almost 4 vol points. On Friday the same tenor rose almost 2 vol points.
Gamma has not repriced to the same extent as vol and skew. The straddle through Wednesday's close covering the midterms implied 1.51%, less than Friday's 1.82% S&P decline alone.

Pre-midterm affordability baskets: long ACA-exposed beneficiaries (GSHLCACA), short drug-makers (GSHLCBPH), long renewables, grid and power names, buy protection on hyperscalers and datacenter equipment, long government-spending exposed ex-defense vs short defense spending beneficiaries, and a corporate tax theme.
TMT: NDX matched its biggest monthly decline since the start of the AI cycle, down about 7% in October. Semis fell about 8% on Friday, the 3rd largest day of underperformance in more than 15 years.

TMT drivers: mixed Kioxia guide, large INTC guide down, uneven 2H hyperscaler capex and an AMKR smartphone downtick. The desk says token demand and gigawatt datacenter build-outs remain intact, but the market is questioning the linearity of the story beyond CY27 and compressing multiples.
Investors are struggling to find rotation names outside Semis/AI. IBM, AAPL, SPOT, V/MA, EBAY and LYV traded well on the week and month.

Financials: the debate is where the cycle stands and how much of it depends on the AI infrastructure buildout. Banks and capital markets stocks were sold, and insurance stayed shorted as P&C earnings showed pricing pressure.
Most-debated financial earnings: LPLA, senior housing REITs, SPGI (strategic review), MA and AMP. GPN was topical Friday on FT reports of takeout interest. Next week: APO, MET and AFRM.

Industrials rose 210bps on the week and are above 300bps month to date, while the broader market fell 50bps. Winners: HAYW +27%, BAH +14%, TXT +12%, IP +9%, FTV. Losers: OI -22%, DAN -15%, TFII, LSTR and CHRW down 12-14%, BA -9% after lowering the timing of its free cash flow goals.

Healthcare outperformed and XLV hit a fresh all-time high on a defensive bid. Large biopharma led: LLY +7%, REGN +11%, GILD +3.4%, MRK +4%. Medtech updates leaned toward negative surprises on forward guidance.

Chart of the week: S&P broke its medium-term CTA threshold (7544.2) Friday with flows concentrated in buying downside at index level and in Semis. VVIX passed 120, the highest since the Iran/US conflict began.
Chart of the week: as the Russell 2000 rallied, open interest fell $2.1B and 3-month funding cheapened, which the desk reads as orderly short covering with recently added length taking profit.

sector_views.rationale: Sector outperformed and XLV hit an all-time high on a defensive bid, with large biopharma most rewarded for strong earnings. Medtech is the weak spot.
Industrials rose 210bps on the week and are above 300bps month to date, led by defense, aerospace and autos. Transports, data center and airlines lagged.
NDX fell about 7% in October and Semis dropped about 8% Friday. Multiples are compressing until visibility beyond CY27 improves.
Banks and capital markets stocks were sold on cycle concerns, and insurance stayed shorted as P&C pricing is pressured.

earnings_insights: LLY: reported a strong beat on Mounjaro and Zepbound with a guidance raise above an elevated bar, stock +7% (reported week of 10/30).
INTC: reported a large guide down (reported week of 10/30). Kioxia gave a mixed guide and AMKR flagged a smartphone downtick.
Hyperscalers: 2H capex spending was uneven in reported results (week of 10/30).
BA: lowered expectations for the timing of free cash flow goals with Q3 results, stock -9%.
TXT: Q3 report took no charge, which had been expected, stock +12%. IP +9% on signs of a turnaround. FTV rose on a better Q3 and guide update.
HAYW: Q3 beat in an under-owned name, stock +27%. OI -22% and DAN -15% on worse earnings. TFII, LSTR and CHRW fell 12-14%.

Upcoming earnings next week: APO (focus on its AI platform and exposure), MET (renewed life insurance interest vs bear focus on investment portfolio quality) and AFRM (pressured by rising rates, with implications for consumer health and funding costs).

Priced move was smaller than Friday's -1.82% S&P decline alone, so the options market is not pricing in a large event move.
